title: docs(releases): document 16.1.0 and the two changesets released at the 16.0.0 GA cut
body:
Fixes #8917

Dedicated **docs-only** PR on a release-owned surface, authored under the per-card approval in the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-16 on #8917. Two files, no code, no changeset (`skip-changeset`). #8912 is the shape precedent.

The ruling's four scope pins were treated as binding, including the one that decides whether the card was worth approving — **nothing beyond what the changesets state**. Every sentence added below is checkable against a package changelog entry; where a changeset is terse, the page is terse.

## Both measurements re-derived, not copied

The card's numbers came from a dev measurement on #8886 and were treated as a pointer, not an input. Re-run from the package changelogs on this branch:

**Gap 1 — 16.1.0's composition.** 8 changesets: 5 minor (`7b07417`, `9e45b63`, `b20201f`, `db160dd`, `fa006fb`), 3 patch (`212b66a`, `818e6a3`, `d10c4dc`). Headline `9e45b63` = #3366, the `os build` / `os validate` preflight that every `requires` capability has an installable provider in the current edition. **Matches the card.**

**Gap 2 — the GA-cut set.** Ids present in the `## 16.0.0` changelog sections and absent from **both** `## 16.0.0-rc.0` and `## 16.0.0-rc.1`:

| changeset | package | content |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `8ff9210` | spec | `ViewFilterRule` operator enum enforced, legacy aliases normalized (#3373) |
| `db34d54` | console | Console pin refreshed to `9a5f016f7d5c` |

Exactly `{db34d54, 8ff9210}` — **the ruling's pin 2 was written against a current reading**, nothing to reconcile.

One methodological note, because it could have hidden a third entry: a changelog "id" is the short sha of the commit that *added* the changeset, so one commit adding two changeset files yields two entries under one id (`bfa3c3f` is such a case — a console pin bump and the `transactionalBatch` capability bit). The arithmetic was therefore re-run keyed on **id + entry text**, not id alone: rc.0 = 86 distinct entries, rc.1 = 16, union 102; the GA section holds 104 and re-lists all 102 (0 rc entries missing — the `changeset pre exit` signature #8912 identified). The 2 GA-only entries are the two above under either key.

## Gap 1 — 16.1.0, folded into `v16.mdx` in the v15 house style

`v15.mdx` folds its minor with three moving parts, and this follows all three:

1. a `## Highlights — 15.1.0` bullet block directly after the major's highlights, above the `---`;
2. a `# What's new in 15.1.0` detail section after the major's detail, with an opener stating the minor's changeset composition;
3. one `###` sub-head per release inside a shared `## Upgrade checklist` at the end.

So `v16.mdx` gains `## Highlights — 16.1.0` (6 bullets, matching v15.1's 6), `# What's new in 16.1.0` (new capabilities / behavior changes & fixes / Console), and `### 16.1.0` in the upgrade checklist. Two consequential edits fall out: the release-status blockquote's sentence "the 16.1.0 minor is not covered here" would have become false, so it now points at the new section; and the page description says "16.0.0 and 16.1.0", as v15's says "15.0.0 and 15.1.0".

**On `index.mdx`** — the ruling offers "a short 16.1.0 section **or** index-entry sentence", and the v15 precedent has both: its index entry carries a "15.1 adds …" clause while `v16`'s says only "(final release: 16.1.0)". I did both rather than pick, since the index entry is itself a release page and the clause is changeset-derived like the rest — flagging it here as a deliberate call rather than leaving it to be discovered. If the reviewer reads the pin as exclusive, the `index.mdx` hunk is a one-line revert and the rest stands.

The checklist entry is not decoration: three of 16.1.0's five minors add a new `os build` / `os validate` gate (#3366, #3367, #3365), so a stack that built clean on 16.0.0 can fail on 16.1.0 — and `runAs:'user'` flows change behavior in a security-relevant direction (#3356).

## Gap 2 — a new `## Landed at the 16.0.0 GA cut` section

The existing `## Landed since 16.0.0-rc.0` window is explicitly scoped to what rolled into `16.0.0-rc.1`, so these two do not belong inside it; they get a sibling section stating plainly that they are in the GA changelog sections and in neither RC. Per the ruling, `8ff9210` is labeled an **accept-set narrowing on a published surface** in its own bold lead.

## Out-of-scope finding — filed as #9035, not addressed here

Chaining each rc.1 console entry's own `objectui range` line to derive the pin at the GA cut turned up a factual error on this same page: `v16.mdx` names `af1b0db` as the `16.0.0-rc.1` Console pin in four places, but rc.1 contains four pin bumps chaining `94d4876df090 → 0318118e02fd → 3b2e4d98d904 → af1b0db96e44 → 69fa5d163a97`, so `af1b0db` is an intermediate and the endpoint is `69fa5d163a97`. Consequence: objectui#2743 (the Console half of the mark-as-read fix whose framework half #3354 the page does document) appears nowhere.

**Not fixed here** — this card is completeness, that is correctness, and the ruling and the dispatch both keep the lanes apart. It does explain an apparent seam a reviewer will notice: the `db34d54` line item states its range as `69fa5d163a97...9a5f016f7d5c`, exactly as the changeset does, which does not meet the `af1b0db` the page states four lines up. The changeset is right; the page is wrong, and #9035 remains open to correct it.

## Verification

Gate union re-derived from the real changed paths — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs content/docs/releases/v16.mdx content/docs/releases/index.mdx` — and run at **`422f086c2`**, the head commit of this branch, with a clean tree. Judged by exit status:

| gate | exit | note |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `pnpm check:docs-audit-scope` | 0 | 9 release-owned pages in scope and review-only |
| `pnpm check:release-notes` | 0 | every released major has a curated, navigable page |
| `pnpm check:release-page-status` | 0 | both in-scope GA majors' status blockquote **and** index entry describe a shipped release — this gate did not exist when #8912 ran, and it reads both surfaces this PR edits |
| `pnpm check:role-word` | 0 | 43 baselined files, no new occurrences |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | 0 | 5952 text files, no raw control bytes |
| `pnpm check:doc-anchors` | 0 | 233 internal fragment links resolve, including the new `#whats-new-in-1610` |
| `pnpm check:doc-authoring` | 0 | 376 files, no bare metadata literals |

The first four are the derivation's own output; `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-anchors` and `check:doc-authoring` were added on top — the middle one because this PR adds an internal fragment link, which is the failure this diff could plausibly introduce. Anchor targets were pre-computed with the same `github-slugger` the gate and the renderer share.

Beyond the gates, both changed files were compiled with the workspace's `@mdx-js/mdx@3.1.1` and produce JSX (113,341 and 7,295 bytes) — MDX is stricter than the markdown the gates parse, and this diff adds inline code containing `{ … }` and `< …>`. Untouched `v15.mdx` was compiled in the same run as a positive control, so a green result is not a no-op instrument.

No `--amend`, no force-push. Left unqueued for the PM to arm.
